videos.title: Give your AI perfect memory in 3 steps
videos.description:
Free Cowork Toolkit: https://coworkacademy.ai/toolkit?utm_source=youtube&utm_medium=shortform&utm_campaign=ig061

Your #AI has three levels of memory (and each one solves a different problem).

1. Built-in memory (in ChatGPT, Claude, or Gemini) handles broad preferences like your role and writing style. It stays high-level because it can influence every chat.
2. Projects keep detailed preferences inside one area of work, so the AI can create detailed memories without mixing in unrelated context. If you prefer three bullet points per slide, it can apply that across every presentation in the Project.
3. ChatGPT Work, Claude Cowork, and Gemini Spark let you decide what gets written down while the AI handles the grunt work. There is a learning curve (but this level gives you the most control).

videos.title: Wim Hof's 2 Minute Routine for More Energy than Coffee
videos.description:
You don't need years to learn to control your immune system. Wim Hof got it down from ten days, to four days, to half an hour.

In this clip, Wim Hof and Jay Shetty talk about the study where people injected with bacteria that should have made them feverish and vomiting simply didn't get sick, and what that says about how much of your body you were told you can't reach.

Wim breaks down the whole method in about a minute: thirty full breaths, exhale, and wait. He explains what happens in the brain stem when your oxygen drops, why that triggers an adrenaline spike bigger than a first-time bungee jump, and what five times more blood flow does to a heart and a brain.

Learn about the man who did 15 push-ups, breathed for one round, and did 40, and why Wim says anxiety isn't a flaw in you but a signal telling you to clean up before you go up.

JAY'S DAILY WISDOM DELIVERED STRAIGHT TO YOUR INBOX

videos.title: 7 Grok Bot agents I use every day
videos.description:
I’m running about 30 active agents at any given moment, and in this episode I break down my full Grok Bot setup: what it is, how it compares to OpenClaw, and the nine bots I’ve built for work and my personal life. We go deep on Chief (my chief-of-staff bot sweeping six inboxes and multiple Slack workspaces), TradBot (the family agent that prints a kitchen-table newspaper for my kids), two engineering bots handling my PR queue and SOC 2 compliance monitoring, Holly Helpdesk, and a handful of personal bots I didn’t expect to actually love. I also walk through how I migrated everything from OpenClaw, including the script I used to export and transplant each agent’s identity and schedule.

*What you’ll learn:*
1. The three primitives Grok Bot is built on, and why one of them changes what agents can actually do
2. How Chief, my general-purpose chief of staff, handles a scope I didn’t think a single bot could manage
3. The writing quirk I noticed immediately with the Grok model, and what I did about it before letting it near my inbox
4. Why I created a family agent, what it produces every morning, and the design principle I used that has nothing to do with a screen
5. The two engineering bots doing work I used to do myself, and how one of them handles compliance in a way that surprised me
6. How Holly Helpdesk started getting five-star reviews from customers who had no idea they were talking to a bot
7. The personal bots I built mostly on a whim, and the one I now look forward to every Monday morning

*My bot templates:* https://x.com/clairevo/status/2093496602522714362

*Brought to you by:*
WorkOS—Make your app enterprise-ready, with SSO, SCIM, RBAC, and more: https://workos.com?utm_source=lennys_howiai&utm_medium=podcast&utm_campaign=q22025
Hyperagent—Deploy fleets of agents that handle real work: https://www.hyperagent.com/howiai

*In this episode, we cover:*
(00:00) Why I migrated from OpenClaw to Grok Bot
(02:10) Grok Bot overview: the three core primitives
(07:41) Chief: my chief-of-staff bot
(11:51) OpenClaw vs. Grok Bot

(32:54) How to migrate your OpenClaws
(34:26) Final take
